AI Agents on "Low-End" Hardware #1

A local AI research agent running on a nearly 16-year-old CPU and a GPU with just 4GB of VRAM.

Hardware:
Core i5-650
8GB DDR3 RAM
AMD Radeon RX 570 4GB

Model: Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M
Context window: 32K tokens
Backend: llama.cpp (Vulkan)
Agent: OpenCode with web search

Running a 4B model with a 32K context window on just 4GB of VRAM is a balancing act, especially when processing large amounts of retrieved information.

The task: Find three scientific sources about photorespiration, explain the biochemical mechanism, and describe the role of RuBisCO.

The result? Three real scientific papers, the biochemical pathway in the correct order, and a largely accurate explanation of RuBisCO's role. All in German, as requested.

Total runtime: 13 minutes and 58 seconds. The agent processed around 18127 prompt tokens, including the retrieved literature.

There were some bibliographic and scientific precision errors, but no fundamental breakdown in understanding. Small models can already handle complex scientific topics, even if the details still need human verification.

What really fascinates me is how far 4B models have come. They can research, use tools, connect information and act as surprisingly capable AI agents.

And this is only the beginning. Efficient architectures and better quantization could put personal local AI within reach of almost everyone.

No cloud. No expensive hardware.

Just a nearly 15-year-old PC showing what is already possible.
